headline: Denied appeal of property tax assessment for 1 Bay Avenue filed by John J. Harris, Trustee
summary: The Board of Assessment Review heard an appeal of the tax assessment on 1 Bay Avenue, CBL: 083A R001001, filed by John J. Harris on behalf of owners Peter & Diana Harris. After presentations and deliberation, the Board voted to deny the appeal, finding the appellant did not prove the assessment was overvalued or that the Assessor made a manifest error. The Board also authorized its attorney to prepare a written decision.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 4, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting by a 3-0 roll call vote.
Found the Board had jurisdiction over the appeal, approved 3-0.
Accepted additional materials submitted by John Harris into the record, 3-0.
Admitted the City's parcel viewer as appellant's Exhibit C into the official record, 3-0.
Denied the appeal of the assessment of 1 Bay Avenue, finding the appellant did not meet their burden of proof, 3-0.
Authorized the Board's Attorney to prepare a written decision to be reviewed and signed within 10 days, approved 3-0.

plain_text:
Board of Assessment Review 
Monday, August 17, 2026, 1:00 PM 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Eric Larsson, Chair 
Dale Knapp 
Lee Lowry 
Samuel Rains, Alternate 
 
The meeting convened at 1:01 p.m. on August 17, 2026 in Room 24 at Portland City Hall, 389 
Congress Street, Portland, Maine. 
 
Attendees: Board members Eric Larsson, Chair, Dale Knapp, Lee Lowry, Samuel Rains, 
Attorney Jonathan Hunter representing the board, City Assessor Elisa Marr, Attorney for the city 
Michael Goldman, appellant John Harris, and board assistant Annie James.  
No members of the public attended. Board attendance was taken by roll call. 
 
Approve the Minutes of the August 4, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting 
Board Chair Larsson moved to approve the minutes of the August 4, 2026 Board of Assessment 
Review Meeting. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call 
vote of (3-0). 
 
Appeal of Assessment of 1 Bay Avenue, CBL: 083A R001001, Owners Peter & Diana 
Harris, Filed by John J. Harris Trustee & Authorized Representative 
 
Board Chair Larsson opened the appeal of the assessment of 1 Bay Avenue, CBL: 083A 
R001001. Board Chair Larsson discussed the role of the Board’s members and alternates, 
introduced the parties, and reviewed the meeting’s agenda. Board Chair Larsson moved to find 
the Board had jurisdiction and Board member Lowry seconded, which was approved by a roll 
call vote of (3-0). The following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Annie James, Attorney Hunter, 
Samuel Rains, Attorney Goldman, John Harris. 
 
Samuel Rains departed the meeting at 1:06 p.m. 
 
Board Chair Larsson reviewed the meeting agenda and the submitted materials. There were no 
objections to the submitted materials. John Harris requested to submit additional material, and 
distributed paper copies to the Assessor, who reviewed and had no objections to the submission 
of the additional materials. Board Chair Larsson moved to accept the additional materials to the
record, which was seconded by Lee Lowry and passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). Paper copies 
of the additional materials were submitted to the Board. The following individuals spoke: Eric 
Larsson, John Harris, Attorney Goldman, Attorney Hunter. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the appellant to present their argument. John Harris, representing 
the appellant, presented his argument, and, when finished, answered questions. During his 
presentation, John Harris distributed paper copies of the City’s parcel viewer, which Board 
member Lowry moved to admit as appellant’s Exhibit C into the official record. Board Chair 
Larsson seconded the motion, which was passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). The following 
individuals spoke: John Harris, Eric Larsson, Attorney Goldman, Attorney Hunter, Annie James, 
Lee Lowry, Dale Knapp. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Assessor’s Exhibit 5, 9. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the Assessor to present their response, and when finished, answered 
questions. The following individuals spoke: Attorney Goldman, Elisa Marr, Dale Knapp, Lee 
Lowry, John Harris, Eric Larsson. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Assessor’s Exhibit 1, the Assessor’s 
Response, Assessor’s Exhibits 7, 9, 8, Appellant’s Exhibit B. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the appellant to close their argument. The following individuals 
spoke: John Harris. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the Assessor to close their argument. The following individuals 
spoke: Attorney Goldman. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the appellant to rebut. The following individuals spoke: John Harris. 
 
Attorney Hunter provided a summary of the Board’s role as the decision-making body. The 
following individuals spoke: Attorney Hunter. 
 
Board Chair Larsson opened the hearing to public comment. No members of the public were 
present.  
 
The Board closed the public portion of the meeting and began their deliberations. The following 
individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Lee Lowry, Dale Knapp, Attorney Hunter. 
 
Board Chair Larsson moved to deny the appeal based on the finding that the Applicant did not 
meet their burden of proving the assessment was substantially overvalued resulting in an 
injustice, or in showing manifest error in the Assessor’s computation of fair market or just value. 
The motion was seconded by Board member Lowry and approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
 
The Board continued discussing the factual findings of the appeal. The following individuals 
spoke: Eric Larsson, John Harris, Jonathan Hunter, Lee Lowry, Dale Knapp. 
 
Elisa Marr departed at 2:36 p.m.
Board Chair Larsson motioned to authorize the Board’s Attorney to prepare a written decision to 
be reviewed and signed within 10 days. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which 
passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). 
New Business (If Necessary) 
 
The Board discussed upcoming schedule. The following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Annie 
James. 
 
Adjournment 
 
Board member Lowry moved and Board Chair Larsson seconded the motion to adjourn, which 
passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). The meeting concluded at 2:58 p.m.
